newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bavarian state chief - delay EMU till criteria met.
newsitem.headline: Bavarian state chief - delay EMU till criteria met.

text.p: Edmund Stoiber, president of the large southern German state of Bavaria, said on Wednesday that Europe's single currency should be delayed until participants adhered strictly to economic entry criteria.
"Economic and monetary union (EMU) either begins on January 1, 1999 as a union of stability, or it must be delayed until the preconditions are met," Stoiber said in a speech in Munich.

Stoiber further warned France against upsetting the "consensus of stability" on which the project is built and which is enshrined in the stability pact, a German initiative aimed at helping the future euro to be a stable currency.

"I can only hope that the stability pact remains unadulterated," he added, referring to doubts as to whether France's newly-elected Socialist government would ratify the pact as agreed by EU ministers in Dublin last December.

The Bavarian Christian Social Union (CSU) party, in which Stoiber is a senior figure, earlier outlined its European stance ahead of next week's EU summit in Amsterdam, stating that any delay to EMU could jeopardise the whole project.
Finance Minister Theo Waigel, leader of the CSU, has repeatedly said he wants a strict interpretation of the EMU entry criteria, despite Germany's own difficulty in a meeting them.
